quality.title: Trusting your computing with Lance and Anton

brief.overview: “Today, Open Source Security is talking to Lance and Anton, the founders of Caution,”
brief.detail:
“Today, Open Source Security is talking to Lance and Anton, the founders of Caution,”
“the secure hosting platform.”
“Lance and Anton are here to talk about verifiable computing today, which I'm really excited”

chapters.title: “Today, Open Source Security is talking to Lance and Anton, the founders of Caution,”
chapters.description: “Today, Open Source Security is talking to Lance and Anton, the founders of Caution,”

chapters.title: Trust and the Compiler Challenge
chapters.description: Exploring the problem of trusting software binaries, Ken Thompson's trusting trust, and the importance of reproducible builds.

chapters.title: Bootstrapping Compilers from Scratch
chapters.description: Detailed explanation of starting from minimal machine code to build full compilers deterministically to establish trusted toolchains.

chapters.title: Limitations and Real-World Attacks
chapters.description: Discussion on challenges Auditing large compilers and real-world supply chain attacks like Xcode Ghost.

chapters.title: Formal Verification and Future Prospects
chapters.description: Potential for applying formal mathematical proofs to LLVM IR and software to deepen trust and correctness guarantees.

chapters.title: “And what verifiable compute is, is actually,”
chapters.description: “And what verifiable compute is, is actually,”

chapters.title: “Yeah, so it's about...”
chapters.description: “Yeah, so it's about...”

chapters.title: Investing in Confidential Computing and Live Memory Snapshots
chapters.description: Discussing investments in confidential computing technology that enables live RAM snapshots for ongoing attestation, with current focus on Intel platforms and the challenge of AMD support.

chapters.title: From Verified Boot to Real-Time Attestation
chapters.description: Exploring limitations of code verification only at boot and describing emerging methods for real-time, ongoing proofs of software integrity at runtime.

chapters.title: Building Minimal Hardened Kernels for Security
chapters.description: Explanation of using minimal, hardened kernels to reduce exploitable boundaries and increase confidence in running code and its privileges.

chapters.title: Use Cases: Crypto Custodians and Privacy-Conscious Services
chapters.description: Examples of high-risk use cases like crypto custodians needing multi-party verification without exposing secrets, and VPN providers proving no-logging policies through verifiable compute.

chapters.title: Easing Adoption through Containerization and Familiar Workflows
chapters.description: Efforts to simplify use by running standard containerized apps like Nginx in enclaves, lowering friction and maintaining developer workflows, broadening security benefits to many.

chapters.title: Open Source Tooling and Reproducible Software Stacks
chapters.description: Describing open source projects like StageX providing supply chain security benefits and verifiable computing that users can reproduce and verify.

chapters.title: Vision for Verifiable Computing as an Internet Standard
chapters.description: Advocating making verifiable computing standard practice to prove running software integrity, enhancing privacy and trust without user friction.
